title: Hands of God
teaser: Across two operating rooms running in lockstep—and one late-night rehearsal where Surgical Chief Emiko Mido lies awake on the operating table under Ryuji's scalpel for the very first time—two pairs of hands save two best friends and redefine their rivalry.
gallery_caption: After placing herself awake beneath Ryuji Sakaguchi's blade to hone his feel for hilar anatomy, Emiko Mido leads Donor Room 1 while Ryuji commands Recipient Room 2 in a synchronized living-donor right-lobe liver transplant—choosing afterward to guard the operating line beside him rather than vie for the Chief's chair.

speakers.杉村弘子 ＆ 薗田愛実 ＆ 深山佳織: Hiroko Sugimura & Itsumi Sonoda & Kaori Miyama

choices.choice_em5_c1_a: "You've followed this case for half a year—why not pair with Deputy Chief Pendragon on the recipient room?"
choices.choice_em5_c1_b: "Simultaneous donor hepatectomy and recipient explant-reconstruction isn't a lead-and-assistant dynamic."
choices.choice_em5_c2_a: "I've confirmed both the pulse and the sheath plane with my own fingertips. The field is in my hands—let me make this call."
choices.choice_em5_c2_b: "I already eased the retractor tension to re-verify in situ—it really is a retrocholedochal course. Leave the dissection to me."
choices.choice_em5_c3_a: "Don't force the native stump together—dissect the proper hepatic artery along the adventitia down to the gastroduodenal bifurcation and fashion a tension-free branch-patch anastomosis."
choices.choice_em5_c3_b: "Release the fibrous band behind the bile duct first to gain arterial length, bypass the most edematous distal intima, and fashion a beveled anastomosis at the healthy bifurcation."
choices.choice_em5_c4_a: "'If'? Here I thought once Chief Mido gave her blessing, the Chief of Surgery post was practically in my pocket."
choices.choice_em5_c4_b: "With the Surgical Chief watching every operating table right beside me, I wouldn't dare slack off for a single day even if I took that seat."

nodes.em5_s1_1_01: At six-thirty in the evening, there was no cup of gone-cold black coffee sitting in the Surgical Chief's office as usual—instead, an entire bank of glaringly bright 3D hepatic CT angiograms and cholangiography films lined the lightboxes.
nodes.em5_s1_1_02: When Ryuji Sakaguchi pushed open the door, Emiko Mido was standing before the illuminators with her arms folded. Catching his footsteps, she skipped any pleasantries and tapped a slender index finger against two thick chart binders on her desk—one stamped in red with "Donor," the other in blue with "Recipient."
nodes.em5_s1_1_03: "Close the door, Sakaguchi. Come take a look at two files I've been tracking for six full months."
nodes.em5_s1_1_04: Ryuji eased the door shut, stepped up to the desk, and opened the blue-covered recipient file.
nodes.em5_s1_1_05: "Naomi Miyahara, twenty-two, fourth-year university student on medical leave... decompensated cirrhosis secondary to autoimmune hepatitis, complicated by recurrent ascites and coagulopathy. Both her MELD score and hepatic reserve have reached the threshold where transplantation is the only option left."
nodes.em5_s1_1_06: He flipped open the red-covered donor binder beside it, his gaze pausing over the blood-type box and volumetric analysis sheet:
nodes.em5_s1_1_07: "Haruko Takase, twenty-two, fourth-year student at the same university—unmarried, unrelated best friend and dorm roommate. Both young women happen to be rare A Rh-negative... That coincidence alone is remarkable enough. Even rarer is the string of workup results behind it: completely normal liver function, no significant steatosis or infectious contraindications, 3D CT volumetry projecting a remnant liver ratio above thirty-eight percent after right hemihepatectomy, and an estimated graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR) well within target for Naomi."
nodes.em5_s1_1_08: "Sharing A Rh-negative certainly makes it simpler for Transfusion Medicine to coordinate compatible blood, though for living-donor liver transplantation, matching blood type only clears the ABO barrier—Rh status isn't what decides whether someone can donate a liver. What actually qualifies her for the table is parenchymal quality, sufficient graft volume for the recipient, an uncompromisingly safe remnant ratio for the donor, and a viable resection-and-reconstruction plan for every branch of the hepatic artery, portal vein, hepatic veins, and bile duct. Miss even one of those, and I would never let a healthy young woman onto a donor table."
nodes.em5_s1_1_09: "Independent psychological evaluation, donor voluntariness verification, and Ethics Committee review... all cleared too?"
nodes.em5_s1_1_10: "The final ethics sign-off came back yesterday afternoon. Those two girls have been inseparable since moving into the same freshman dorm room—normally it was always calm, meticulous Naomi looking after scatterbrained Haruko, right up until their short graduation trip to the coast six months ago, when Naomi suddenly developed severe jaundice and impending esophageal variceal bleeding at their inn and came straight into my ER shift by ambulance."
nodes.em5_s1_1_11: Studying the two starkly different livers on the lightbox, Emiko let the corner of her cool lips curve by the faintest fraction, as though recalling the absurd scene of her very first meeting with the pair half a year earlier.
nodes.em5_s1_2_01: The instant twenty-two-year-old university senior Haruko Takase heard that Naomi had rare A Rh-negative blood—and that her own lab slip showed the exact same type—she shot out of her chair, thumped her chest, and yanked her sleeve all the way past her elbow:
nodes.em5_s1_2_02: "That's amazing, Dr. Mido! Isn't Naomi's A Rh-negative blood super rare? I'm A-negative too! How much blood do you need from me? Will four hundred milliliters do it? If that's not enough, I'll drink two extra bowls of sweet red-bean soup and come back next month for another draw!"
nodes.em5_s1_2_03: Behind the desk, Emiko Mido expressionlessly slid a standard open hepatectomy anatomical diagram right under her nose, tapping the cold nib of her fountain pen along the long reversed-L subcostal incision line on the right:
nodes.em5_s1_2_04: "Roll your sleeve down first, Miss Takase. Having the same blood type doesn't mean you qualify as a liver donor—and transfusing blood won't save a liver that has already gone into widespread fibrotic decompensation. What we are discussing is living-donor liver transplantation: opening your abdomen under general anesthesia, resecting the right half of your healthy liver, and transplanting it into her body."
nodes.em5_s1_2_05: Haruko's hand froze mid-air at her elbow. She blinked twice, half-convinced her ears were playing tricks on her:
nodes.em5_s1_2_06: "...Huh? C-cut out my liver?! Hold on, Doctor—I thought matching meant drawing a few tubes of blood! You really mean slicing my stomach open that wide with a scalpel and cutting a piece of an organ out of me?!"
nodes.em5_s1_2_07: "Yes. Although a healthy adult's remnant liver regenerates postoperatively, this is a major open abdominal operation carrying real risks of hemorrhage, bile leak, and even death. This hospital never accepts impulsive heroics."
nodes.em5_s1_2_08: Every trace of color drained from Haruko's face. Hands and feet turning ice-cold as she stared at the branching portal veins and bile ducts on the sheet, her voice began to shake:
nodes.em5_s1_2_09: "M-my knees go weak just getting local anesthetic for a wisdom tooth... I'm sorry, Dr. Mido, could I... could I go home and think about this...?"
nodes.em5_s1_2_10: Haruko practically walked out of the consultation room moving the same arm and leg together; and the moment Naomi Miyahara heard about it up on the ward, she grabbed Haruko's hands and flatly refused to let her healthy best friend take a blade like that for her sake.
nodes.em5_s1_2_11: Emiko had assumed that would be the end of the living-donor inquiry.
nodes.em5_s1_2_12: Yet barely a single week later—right as morning clinic opened on the seventh day—Haruko Takase knocked on Emiko's door alone, sporting faint dark circles under her eyes and clutching a thick notebook bristling with sticky notes and hand-copied medical definitions.
nodes.em5_s1_2_13: "Dr. Mido, I spent the whole week reading every liver-transplant guide I could borrow from the medical library... Honestly, I still woke up twice last night from nightmares about the operating table."
nodes.em5_s1_2_14: Both hands gripped the edge of the notebook until her knuckles turned white, yet her gaze no longer wavered:
nodes.em5_s1_2_15: "But for more than three years—whether I botched course registration or collapsed with a fever—Naomi was always the one cleaning up my messes. If I actually have a chance to save her and I shrink back just because I'm scared of pain... I'll never forgive myself for the rest of my life. Please put me through formal donor screening. This is my own decision!"
nodes.em5_s1_3_01: "Scared off for a week, yet she researched every risk on her own, walked right back in, endured six straight months of grueling workups and independent voluntariness interviews—and turned out to be an ideal clinical match on top of it... That young woman has real grit. Did Naomi agree too?"
nodes.em5_s1_3_02: "At first Naomi refused point-blank to sign the recipient consent. The two of them shut the ward door and had a massive argument, until Naomi came out red-eyed and told me—'Since Haruko made up her mind after thinking everything through seriously, crying and pushing it away would only trample on her courage. I have to live well and pay her back with interest.' Compared to patients who do nothing but weep and apologize, I much prefer a clear-headed recipient like her."
nodes.em5_s1_3_03: Turning to pick up red and blue markers, Emiko briskly wrote two columns across the surgical scheduling whiteboard: "Operating Room 1" and "Operating Room 2."
nodes.em5_s1_3_04: "The operation is set for next week. Adult-to-adult living-donor right-lobe liver transplantation—two operating rooms opening simultaneously, interlocking every phase to the minute. It's the weightiest hepatobiliary transplant Hoshimi Hospital will perform all year."
nodes.em5_s1_3_05: She wrote her own name under Operating Room 1 (Donor: Haruko Takase), then pivoted and leveled the tip of the blue marker straight at Ryuji Sakaguchi:
nodes.em5_s1_3_06: "I will lead the open right donor hepatectomy in Room 1, where the cardinal law is absolute protection of healthy donor Haruko Takase's remnant perfusion, middle hepatic vein outflow, and zero biliary injury. Next door in Room 2—total native hepatectomy, inferior vena cava outflow venoplasty, and graft vascular and biliary reconstruction for recipient Naomi Miyahara—Sakaguchi, you're primary surgeon."
nodes.em5_s1_3_07: Ryuji's gaze sharpened slightly as he looked at the two side-by-side operating rooms on the whiteboard.
nodes.em5_c1a_01: "You've spent half a year preparing this case. Purely in terms of open hepatobiliary seniority, Deputy Chief Artoria is right here in the department—I expected you two to split the rooms."
nodes.em5_c1a_02: "Spare me the probing look. Pendragon's hepatobiliary blade work is unquestionably top-tier; vying with her for Chief has never made me underestimate her skill, and I would certainly never stall a patient's schedule over personal pride—the past six months went to stabilizing Naomi's autoimmune markers and completing every ethics review."
nodes.em5_c1a_03: Lifting her chin, she locked her cool gaze unflinchingly onto Ryuji's eyes:
nodes.em5_c1a_04: "It just so happens both workups matured now, and your hands have reached the height required to catch this case. When two surgeons are equally qualified... for an operation where we stand back-to-back entrusting patients' lives to each other, I would rather do it with you. Any objections?"
nodes.em5_c1b_01: "One room harvesting a right lobe from a healthy young woman without a millimeter's margin for error, the other stripping out a decompensated cirrhotic liver and anastomosing portal vein, hepatic artery, and bile duct within minimal cold ischemia time... Neither room has anywhere to retreat."
nodes.em5_c1b_02: "Good—you understand the stakes. Laypeople always assume the recipient room just sews in whatever liver arrives, or conversely that the donor room is merely fetching a spare part. In reality, the donor cannot suffer even a one-percent risk of remnant failure, while recipient explantation and microvascular reconstruction under portal hypertension and coagulopathy walk a razor's edge at every stitch."
nodes.em5_c1b_03: Her lips curved faintly with the poised pride of an elite Surgical Chief:
nodes.em5_c1b_04: "I have never needed a man who only knows how to stand behind me holding retractors. For six months I've waited until this hospital could field two genuinely equal teams—one I never have to glance over my shoulder to babysit. Now, the lead spot in the second room is yours."
nodes.em5_s1m_01: Reaching out to take the blue marker, Ryuji signed his name steadily under primary surgeon for Operating Room 2.
nodes.em5_s1m_02: "Understood. Operating Room 2—recipient Naomi Miyahara. I'll take the lead."
nodes.em5_s1m_03: "Good. The most treacherous hurdle on the recipient side will be dissecting Naomi's hilar plate—edematous and distorted after chronic hepatitis—and controlling tension across a hair-fine hepatic artery anastomosis. Studying 3D reconstructions alone won't give your fingertips the feel of a living arterial sheath pulsing beneath them."
nodes.em5_s1m_04: Snapping the chart binder shut, Emiko glanced at the wall clock, her tone as matter-of-fact as if announcing routine morning rounds:
nodes.em5_s1m_05: "So tomorrow night at eight, after hours, report to Operating Room 1. Don't schedule any other plans—I've arranged one final hands-on rehearsal before the transplant."
nodes.em5_s1m_06: "Tomorrow night at eight? Where did a training patient come from?"
nodes.em5_s1m_07: At the door, hand resting on the lever, Emiko glanced back; an almost imperceptible tautness flickered across her striking features before she pressed it down beneath an unmistakable tone of command:
nodes.em5_s1m_08: "You'll know once you're in the operating room."
nodes.em5_s2_01: Eight o'clock at night. Overhead lights blazed across Operating Room 1.
nodes.em5_s2_02: Hiroko Sugimura had already laid out a fine hepatobiliary vascular dissection set across the sterile table; twenty-year-old circulating nurse Itsumi Sonoda was carefully checking warmed irrigation saline and ECG leads, while Kaori Miyama loosened her wrists beside the lightbox.
nodes.em5_s2_03: "Hiroko-senpai, Dr. Miyama... Chief Mido specifically called just the few of us in tonight, and the wards haven't sent down an operative slip... Think she's giving us a pop drill on instrument passing for next week's living-donor transplant? My palms are already sweating..."
nodes.em5_s2_04: "Chief Mido only handed me the internal surgical training filing at dusk. Seeing the hospital's official Staff Surgical Training authorization stamp on it, I assumed one of the junior doctors had volunteered."
nodes.em5_s2_07: Yet Emiko Mido stepped inside wearing no surgical scrubs. Draped loosely over her shoulders was a white doctor's coat—and underneath it, unmistakably, was a standard pale-blue inpatient gown, her jet-black hair—ordinarily pinned up without a stray strand—hanging loose across her shoulders.
nodes.em5_s2_08: Everyone in the room froze at once.
nodes.em5_s2_10: Emiko didn't answer right away. Walking straight to the instrument cabinet, she unclipped the metal nameplate reading "Surgical Chief · Emiko Mido" from the left lapel of her coat, set it flat on the stainless-steel counter with a crisp click, and slipped off the outer white coat, folding it neatly.
nodes.em5_s2_11: "Stop looking toward the door—there is no other patient tonight. I signed and filed the hospital's formal Staff Surgical Training approval and informed consent myself this afternoon."
nodes.em5_s2_12: Turning around, she swept a composed gaze past wide-eyed Itsumi Sonoda, solemn Kaori Miyama, and Hiroko Sugimura before coming to rest squarely on Ryuji Sakaguchi:
nodes.em5_s2_13: "Tonight's procedure is a strictly bounded open upper-abdominal hilar and hepatoduodenal ligament fine-dissection confirmation—zero parenchymal resection, solely live exposure and variant identification of the hilar vessels and biliary sheath, followed by primary closure. Primary surgeon: Ryuji Sakaguchi. First assistant: Miyama. Scrub nurse: Hiroko. Circulating: Sonoda. Anesthesia safety monitoring by the on-call anesthesiologist. And the patient—is me."
nodes.em5_s2_14: "E-eeeh?! C-Chief Mido is getting on the operating table as the patient herself?!"
nodes.em5_s2_15: "Chief, even with the hospital's training protocol in place, you've never once lain on an operating table yourself, have you? Going this far just so Dr. Sakaguchi can calibrate his hilar feel for next week's recipient room..."
nodes.em5_s2_16: "Spare me the melodrama, Miyama. The tissues around Naomi's hepatic artery and portal vein leave zero margin, and plastic models don't give you live arterial pulsation or autonomic reflexes. Since I personally named Sakaguchi to command Operating Room 2, it's my responsibility to make sure his hands are in peak condition before skin incision."
nodes.em5_s2_17: Her reasoning was airtight and every inch commanding—yet as she actually stepped toward the narrow green-draped operating table at the center of the theater, Ryuji caught it immediately: her stride was a full half-beat slower than when she walked up to lead a table herself.
nodes.em5_s2_18: "What are you all standing around for? From this point on, follow standard preoperative protocol as you would for any surgical patient."
nodes.em5_s2_19: Hiroko Sugimura recovered first, stepping forward with poised professionalism:
nodes.em5_s2_20: "Understood. Then... Dr. Mido, please sit up on the operating table first so we can tuck all of your hair inside this surgical cap."
nodes.em5_s2_21: The true reversal of roles only turned starkly real as each preparatory step landed on her own body one by one.
nodes.em5_s2_22: When her long black hair was gathered completely inside the disposable blue patient cap, baring her smooth, slightly tense forehead and the curve of her ears; when, assisted with quiet restraint by Hiroko and Itsumi, she shed the cover of the hospital gown and lay flat on her back atop the cool, firm table pad—the massive shadowless surgical lamp she had spent her career looking down from hung blindingly overhead directly above her own eyes for the first time.
nodes.em5_s2_23: (Gingerly smoothing ECG electrodes onto her chest and clipping the pulse oximeter onto her index finger) "C-Chief... no, Dr. Mido, I've fastened the nylon positioning straps over your armboards—are they too tight?"
nodes.em5_s2_24: Crisp, steady beeps from the cardiac monitor immediately filled the quiet operating room—ninety-two beats per minute, unmistakably faster than the Surgical Chief's usual resting pulse.
nodes.em5_s2_25: Her jawline tightening slightly, Emiko stared straight up at the ceiling and answered stiffly:
nodes.em5_s2_26: "...They're fine. And Sonoda—you don't need to remind me how narrow this table is with every single adjustment."
nodes.em5_s2_28: "As for anesthesia, I am not taking general. I intend to stay awake from start to finish—high thoracic continuous epidural blockade. Anesthesia will verify block level and hemodynamics at the head of the table; as for the puncture and catheter placement... Sakaguchi, you're doing it yourself."
nodes.em5_s2_29: Having verified her preoperative coagulation labs and spinal assessment sheet, the on-call anesthesiologist nodded to Ryuji:
nodes.em5_s2_30: "Vitals and puncture landmarks cleared. The epidural tray is ready, and I'll co-monitor block height continuously from the head side."
nodes.em5_s2_31: Donning sterile gloves after surgical hand prep, Ryuji stepped behind Emiko as she curled onto her side. Even through thin latex, he could feel the muscles along the proud Chief's spine drawn as taut as a bowstring.
nodes.em5_s2_32: "Local infiltration at the T7–T8 interspace—advancing the epidural needle now, Emiko. Ease your back a little; don't fight the tip."
nodes.em5_s2_33: (Face buried in the crook of her arm, voice muffled) "...Do I need you lecturing me on how to position for an epidural? Just thread the catheter."
nodes.em5_s2_34: As the catheter settled cleanly into the epidural space and fractionated test and loading doses of local anesthetic went in, a warm, heavy numbness crept steadily from her costal margin across her upper abdomen and flanks.
nodes.em5_s2_35: Returned to the supine position after Hiroko completed standard preoperative urinary catheterization and positioning checks, even though every colleague in the room observed impeccable clinical decorum without a single stray remark, the unfamiliar vulnerability—losing motor command of her trunk while lying bare across the upper abdomen before her own subordinates as cool povidone-iodine painted wide swaths over her skin—still turned Emiko's knuckles faintly white against the armboard pads.
nodes.em5_s2_36: Chilled alcohol swabs and a blunt testing pin touched her skin in sequence.
nodes.em5_s2_37: "Sensory block stably covers T4 through T12, symmetric bilaterally, zero sharp-pain perception. Blood pressure 118 over 74, heart rate settled back to 82—epidural blockade confirmed adequate."
nodes.em5_s2_38: Layers of sterile green fenestrated drapes went up, partitioning Emiko's head-side view from the upper-abdominal field. Freshly scrubbed and gowned, Ryuji took his stance at the primary surgeon's spot and looked across the low ether screen into her eyes:
nodes.em5_s2_39: "Block verification is complete. Keep your eyes on me—if anything feels remotely sharp, speak up immediately."
nodes.em5_s2_40: "Stop fussing... Make the incision and don't waste time."
nodes.em5_s2_43: The exact instant the steel edge glided smoothly down the marked upper-midline line—
nodes.em5_s2_45: A razor-brief gasp she failed to swallow burst from behind the drape screen, and Emiko's shoulders jolted taut against the table pad!
nodes.em5_s2_46: Ryuji's wrist arrested in midair on the instant without deepening by half a millimeter; Hiroko and the anesthesiologist snapped onto high alert in unison.
nodes.em5_s2_47: "All stop! —Emiko, was that sharp incisional pain just now? Anesthesia, re-verify the T6 dermatomes immediately!"
nodes.em5_s2_48: Two seconds of dead silence hung beneath the shadowless lamps.
nodes.em5_s2_49: While the anesthesiologist swiftly rechecked the sensory borders and hemodynamic waveforms at the head of the table, Emiko drew two quick breaths behind the screen—and her pale, composed cheeks flushed visibly crimson all the way to the tips of her ears and down her neck.
nodes.em5_s2_50: "Dr. Sakaguchi, T4-to-T12 nociceptive block is completely intact—no blood-pressure or heart-rate nociceptive spike. Confirmed zero sharp pain breakthrough."
nodes.em5_s2_51: (Looking down toward the head of the table) "...No sharp pain?"
nodes.em5_s2_52: Behind the sterile screen, Emiko looked ready to wish the floor would swallow her whole; yet with her wrists loosely secured to the armboards, all she could do was bite her lower lip and glare up at Ryuji in mortified, low-voiced frustration:
nodes.em5_s2_53: "...I know it didn't hurt! The block level is perfectly fine!"
nodes.em5_s2_54: Drawing a sharp breath, she tried desperately to summon back her usual lecturing authority, though her burning earlobes thoroughly betrayed the embarrassment of her very first time as a patient:
nodes.em5_s2_55: "I knew perfectly well in my head what was happening—I just didn't expect that the second steel actually parted my skin and I felt the abdominal wall tug, my body would answer for me without asking permission...!"
nodes.em5_s2_56: Beside the Mayo stand, Hiroko kept her eyes dutifully lowered, pressing the faintest twitch of a smile firmly back beneath her surgical mask; at the head side, Itsumi dabbed sweat from the Chief's temple in hushed awe, scarcely daring to breathe.
nodes.em5_s2_57: Taking in her scarlet ears and stubbornly proud gaze, Ryuji didn't tease her—speaking instead in the calm, assured, unhurried cadence of the attending surgeon in charge:
nodes.em5_s2_58: "For anyone lying on this table the first time, a tactile startle reflex couldn't be more normal. —Right now I'm primary surgeon in this room, so Patient Mido only needs to let her shoulders settle back onto the pad and breathe to my voice. Can you do that?"
nodes.em5_s2_59: At that unassuming yet unmistakable "I'm primary surgeon," Emiko blinked for half a beat—and the iron line of her shoulders finally eased millimeter by millimeter back onto the cushion.
nodes.em5_s2_60: (Turning her face slightly aside with a soft huff) "...Understood. Carry on."
nodes.em5_s2_62: After dividing the linea alba and peritoneum layer by layer, Kaori Miyama seated the deep retractors with rock-steady hands, gently elevating the round ligament and inferior hepatic border until the crisp anatomy of the hepatoduodenal ligament lay exposed beneath the lamps.
nodes.em5_s2_63: Past the initial jolt of skin incision, Emiko lying behind the screen soon showed the instincts of a master surgeon—even blind to the field, her focus tracked every quiet click of steel above her:
nodes.em5_s2_64: "Keep reporting, Sakaguchi. Have you palpated the foramen of Winslow yet? Where is the lateral margin of the common hepatic duct, and what pulse are you feeling posterior to it? Don't skip steps just because I'm the one on the table."
nodes.em5_s2_65: "Foramen of Winslow is patent, zero adhesions. Picking up the anterior serosal leaf of the hepatoduodenal ligament with fine atraumatic forceps now—the right lateral border of the common bile duct is clean, and the main portal vein lies posterior and slightly medial with normal turgor and elasticity."
nodes.em5_s2_66: "Good. As you carry the perivascular sheath dissection up toward the hilum, identify the takeoff of the gastroduodenal artery clearly before passing a right-angle clamp deep."
nodes.em5_s2_67: (Murmuring in involuntary admiration) "She can't see a single thing past the sterile drape, yet the Chief is practically sketching the entire anatomical atlas in her head just from listening..."
nodes.em5_s2_68: Yet several millimeters farther along, as Ryuji gently brushed loose areolar tissue off the proper hepatic artery with a peanut sponge to expose the deep origin of the right hepatic artery, his motion slowed slightly.
nodes.em5_s2_69: (Immediately catching the two-second pause in instrument sounds) "Why did you stop? By standard anatomy, the right hepatic artery should be crossing obliquely upward across the anteromedial aspect of the common hepatic duct right now—just incise along the anterior sheath."
nodes.em5_s2_70: Ryuji palpated the subtle deep arterial pulse carefully with the pad of his finger, then exchanged a confirming look across the table with Kaori Miyama:
nodes.em5_s2_71: "No—we can't lift straight up along the anterior wall. Your actual course isn't textbook: your right hepatic artery branches off low and passes directly posterior to the common bile duct, hugging the anterior wall of the portal vein, with a hair-fine caudate-lobe arterial branch running medially beside it."
nodes.em5_s2_72: Behind the drape screen, silence fell at once.
nodes.em5_s2_73: For Emiko Mido—accustomed her entire career to seeing the whole board with her own eyes and issuing the final word—nothing lay before her gaze right now save a sheet of pale-green sterile cloth. She could neither see her own viscera nor reach in to palpate that variant vessel.
nodes.em5_s2_74: "...Are you certain it courses posterior to the duct, and isn't an artifact of local fascial traction?"
nodes.em5_c2a_01: "I've confirmed both the arterial pulse and the sheath plane with my own fingertips, and Miyama has a clear view as well. Emiko—the field is in my hands right now. Let me make this call."
nodes.em5_c2b_01: "I already had Miyama ease the retractor tension so I could re-verify in situ—it's a classic retrocholedochal course, no traction artifact. Trust me to dissect it from the posterolateral plane instead."
nodes.em5_s2m_01: Nothing sounded in the operating room save the calm, even cadence of the pulse monitor.
nodes.em5_s2m_02: Three full seconds passed before a quiet exhale came from behind the sterile drape. This time, the last trace of habitual tension and need for control had melted from Emiko Mido's voice, leaving it calm and crisp:
nodes.em5_s2m_04: With those four words, not a hint of hesitation remained in Ryuji's hands.
nodes.em5_s2m_05: Switching to the finest vascular forceps and silicone vessel loops, he opened the periadventitial plane millimeter by millimeter along the posterolateral margin of the common bile duct—sparing that thread-fine caudate branch untouched while laying out the three-dimensional relationship of portal vein, right hepatic artery, and common hepatic duct in crystal clarity.
nodes.em5_s2m_06: "Not a single drop of ooze... Even the vasa vasorum over the arterial adventitia are completely intact."
nodes.em5_s2m_07: "Three-dimensional hilar triad skeletonization and variant verification complete. Removing silicone vessel loops, warm saline irrigation, preparing for anatomic repositioning and layered closure."
nodes.em5_s2m_08: "Sponge, needle, and instrument counts verified three times—all correct!"
nodes.em5_s2m_09: Half an hour later, the final subcuticular stitch was cinched and trimmed, and a smooth sterile dressing was smoothed into place.
nodes.em5_s2m_10: When the sterile drapes came down and a warmed blanket settled back over her shoulders, Emiko Mido's bangs were faintly damp and her face showed a touch of fatigue after staying awake through an entire open exploration—yet before the stretcher transfer she still mustered her Chief's poise, looking at each of the three staff members beside the table:
nodes.em5_s2m_11: "Miyama's retraction was steady, Hiroko's instrument passing was flawless as ever, and Sonoda's circulating counts were crisp... Good work tonight, all three of you. And no gossiping once you leave this room."
nodes.em5_s2m_13: Only after the three colleagues and the anesthesiologist wheeled the instrument carts out ahead of them and eased the prep-room door shut did Emiko turn her head slightly toward Ryuji beside the bed, her voice pitched low enough for just the two of them:
nodes.em5_s2m_14: "...Back on the table at the first incision—don't you dare file that away to laugh at me later."
nodes.em5_s2m_15: (Tucking the corner of the warm blanket around her with a quiet smile) "Wouldn't dream of it. Patient Mido cooperated admirably tonight."
nodes.em5_s3_01: At seven-fifty the next morning, when Ryuji Sakaguchi nudged open the Surgical Chief's office door carrying two hot coffees, Emiko Mido was already standing impeccably dressed at her desk reviewing the morning handover sheets just like any ordinary workday.
nodes.em5_s3_02: Except that a split second before the door clicked open, her lashes had been lowered, her right hand resting with faint bemusement over the midline of her upper abdomen through her white coat and blouse.
nodes.em5_s3_03: "Morning. Standing up reading reports already? You could've slept another half hour."
nodes.em5_s3_04: Lowering her hand to accept the hot coffee, Emiko glanced down with an odd expression at her completely flat, unblemished abdomen:
nodes.em5_s3_05: "...Even knowing full well how recovery works after years at this hospital, experiencing it firsthand is still surreal. At nine o'clock last night, your retractors had this wide open and you were turning over my hepatoduodenal ligament."
nodes.em5_s3_06: "Any lingering soreness or discomfort anywhere now?"
nodes.em5_s3_07: "Not a trace—it didn't even slow my morning run. If anything, listening to you call out every anatomical layer from behind that drape last night left my own hands itching this morning."
nodes.em5_s3_08: Seeing how brisk and energized she looked, Ryuji leaned against the edge of her desk with a light laugh:
nodes.em5_s3_09: "In that case, how about returning the favor? Once this busy stretch wraps up, I'll lie down on the operating table and let you open me up in return—make up for all the lead-surgeon satisfaction you missed behind the curtain last night."
nodes.em5_s3_10: Emiko's hand paused around her coffee cup, and she shot him a cool sideways look at once:
nodes.em5_s3_11: "Nonsense. Next week is Haruko Takase and Naomi Miyahara's dual-room living-donor liver transplant—what would it look like if our recipient lead surgeon climbed onto an operating table to get cut open beforehand? Rejected."
nodes.em5_s3_12: "Fair point. Next week's transplant comes first."
nodes.em5_s3_13: Just as Ryuji turned to pick up the transplant schedule, Emiko's voice came from behind him—dropped half a shade quieter.
nodes.em5_s3_14: "...That said, I only meant not right now."
nodes.em5_s3_15: Taking a sip of black coffee, she narrowed her cool, striking eyes slightly, looking Ryuji up and down with a glint of dangerous, dead-serious intrigue:
nodes.em5_s3_16: "Laying you flat on that narrow table all by yourself, letting you taste what it's like listening to instruments clink while unable to budge an inch... Someday, I probably really will want to operate on you with my own hands."
nodes.em5_s3_17: "...Sounds like I may have just dug myself quite a pit."
nodes.em5_s3_18: "Too late to get cold feet now. And let me lay down the ground rules in advance—"
nodes.em5_s3_19: Lifting her chin, she delivered each word in her most matter-of-fact Surgical Chief cadence:
nodes.em5_s3_20: "When that day comes, your preoperative prep isn't going to Hiroko, and certainly not to any of the junior nurses. From ward skin prep and catheterization to strapping you onto the table, this Chief will do every step with her own hands."
nodes.em5_s3_21: Silence hung in the office for one full beat.
nodes.em5_s3_22: Having declared it with far too much solemn certainty, Emiko met Ryuji's half-smiling gaze and realized on her own just how fiercely possessive that proclamation had sounded—a thin wash of crimson sweeping straight up her pale ears.
nodes.em5_s3_23: (Setting her coffee mug sharply back onto the desk, expression snapping stern) "...What are you smiling at?! It's strictly to guarantee the surgical field meets my highest sterile standards! If you have nothing else, go verify next week's vascular suture gauges for Operating Room 2—morning conference is about to start!"
nodes.em5_s3_24: Holding back his grin, Ryuji tactfully left it unremarked, picking up his folder and heading for the door:
nodes.em5_s3_25: "Yes, Chief Mido. Next week across those two rooms, we settle things at the table for real."
nodes.em5_s3_26: The door clicked softly shut as morning sunlight fell across the two names written side by side on the whiteboard—six final days remained before the living-donor transplant half a year in the making.
nodes.em5_s4_1_01: Eight o'clock sharp one week later. Lights along the fourth-floor sterile surgical transfer corridor shone bright as noon.
nodes.em5_s4_1_02: Two transport gurneys paused side by side at the fork leading into Operating Room 1 and Operating Room 2.
nodes.em5_s4_1_03: On the left gurney, Naomi Miyahara's complexion carried the pallor and dullness of chronic liver disease, yet her eyes were clear. Turning her head, she reached slender fingers across the gap to brush the back of her best friend Haruko Takase's hand.
nodes.em5_s4_1_04: "Haruko. Before we roll through those doors, let me say it one last time—even right here at the threshold, this is never something you owed me. You were completely healthy, and now you're taking such a massive incision because of me... I don't think I'll ever finish tallying this debt in one lifetime."
nodes.em5_s4_1_05: On the right gurney, ever-breezy Haruko Takase had all her hair tucked inside a blue surgical cap today, her fingers clutching the sheet beneath her tight. Hearing Naomi's words, she craned her neck at once and shot back half an octave louder than usual:
nodes.em5_s4_1_06: "Cut it out with the tearjerker lines already! Truth be told, six months ago when I rolled up my sleeve in clinic, I genuinely thought matching meant donating four hundred milliliters of blood! Who knew Dr. Mido was going to jump straight to slicing half my liver?!"
nodes.em5_s4_1_07: (A helpless, aching fondness flickering in her eyes as she murmured back) "...Idiot. You're the only person in the entire university who'd thump her chest before telling blood donation apart from a liver transplant."
nodes.em5_s4_1_08: "Hmph—well, I looked up every single page myself before signing! Listen up, Naomi: once the two of us roll out of these doors safe and sound, dorm cleaning duty plus ten years of late-night snacks are all on your tab—as for the credits you missed on leave, I can't bail you out there, so stay alive and pass those makeups yourself!"
nodes.em5_s4_1_09: (Lips curving into a gentle, resolute smile) "Deal. Late-night snacks are on me, and I'll earn every credit myself. ...See you soon, Haruko."
nodes.em5_s4_1_11: Parting left and right, the two gurneys glided smoothly into the adjacent Operating Rooms 1 and 2.
nodes.em5_s4_2_01: Without her best friend beside her to trade banter, the moment Haruko Takase was shifted onto the narrow operating table at the center of Operating Room 1—looking up at the massive, cold shadowless lamp dome, rows of glinting abdominal retractors, and ventilator tubing—every ounce of bravado she had mustered in the hall vanished on the spot.
nodes.em5_s4_2_02: Her heart rate on the monitor vaulted straight to one hundred and ten beats per minute. Lips paling, Haruko looked toward Emiko Mido beside the table with an unmistakable tremor in her voice:
nodes.em5_s4_2_03: "D-Dr. Mido... I-I memorized the whole risk sheet backward and forward, b-but lying here staring up at this lamp, my legs won't stop shaking... Are you really about to cut a huge piece of liver out of my stomach? What if I never wake up again...?"
nodes.em5_s4_2_04: Two weeks earlier, strictly metrics-driven Emiko Mido would likely have recited a string of cold safety statistics.
nodes.em5_s4_2_05: Yet right now, looking down at the young woman gripping the armboard cushions beneath the lamp, Emiko vividly recalled that night six days ago—unclipping her own Chief's badge to lie on this exact cold, narrow table, and the jolt of her own pulse when the first blade touched skin.
nodes.em5_s4_2_06: Stepping closer, Emiko looked down at Haruko above her surgical mask—her gaze steady and sharp as ever, yet carrying a genuine warmth rarely heard in her voice:
nodes.em5_s4_2_07: "Lying on a table this cold and narrow, being scared couldn't be more normal. That feeling... I know it firsthand."
nodes.em5_s4_2_08: Haruko blinked in surprise up at the notoriously strict Surgical Chief.
nodes.em5_s4_2_09: "I have rechecked your middle hepatic vein plane and remnant volume more than ten times—not a single millimeter extra will be taken. Miss Takase, you have already finished the step that took the greatest courage. Close your eyes and sleep; leave the rest to my hands."
nodes.em5_s4_2_10: Warmth stinging the taut corners of her eyes, Haruko gave a firm nod:
nodes.em5_s4_2_11: "...Mm! I'm counting on you, Dr. Mido!"
nodes.em5_s4_2_12: As the donor-team anesthesiologist smoothly infused the general-anesthesia induction agents, Haruko's breathing lengthened into a calm, even rhythm.
nodes.em5_s4_3_01: At that exact moment, just beyond the dividing wall in Operating Room 2—
nodes.em5_s4_3_02: Naomi Miyahara quietly cooperated with Kaori Miyama and Hiroko Sugimura through the final pre-induction checks. Just before the oxygen mask settled gently over her face, she looked calmly toward Ryuji Sakaguchi at the primary spot:
nodes.em5_s4_3_03: "Dr. Sakaguchi. Truthfully, Haruko hates pain more than anyone—and today she's sharing such a precious part of her body with me... Please help me receive it safely."
nodes.em5_s4_3_04: "Rest easy, Miss Miyahara. Chief Mido is watching over Haruko next door, and my whole team is watching over you right here. Once you wake up, the two of you still have a graduation to make together."
nodes.em5_s4_3_05: Naomi closed her eyes in quiet reassurance as general anesthesia induction and endotracheal intubation proceeded smoothly.
nodes.em5_s4_3_06: "Operating Room 2 Surgical Time-Out—recipient Naomi Miyahara, twenty-two, blood type A Rh-negative, decompensated cirrhosis secondary to autoimmune hepatitis, scheduled for orthotopic living-donor right-lobe liver transplantation; Transfusion Medicine has verified our blood-readiness plan with A Rh-negative red cells, ABO-compatible plasma, and matched platelets. Sonoda, confirm synchronized timing with Room 1."
nodes.em5_s4_3_07: (Reporting crisply beside the dedicated inter-room intercom) "Chief Mido in Room 1 has completed Time-Out and made skin incision! Per our dual-room protocol, Room 2 proceeds first with laparotomy, perihepatic adhesiolysis, and short hepatic veins along the third porta; once Room 1 confirms graft quality and vascular anatomy in situ and enters the final phase of parenchymal transection, Room 2 will clamp and explant the native liver to compress the anhepatic phase and cold ischemia time to the absolute minimum!"
nodes.em5_s4_3_10: Forty minutes into the operation, progress remained rock-steady.
nodes.em5_s4_3_11: Just as Ryuji and Kaori Miyama were meticulously dividing engorged portal-hypertensive collateral veins across Naomi's abdominal wall and greater omentum, the side door of Operating Room 2 slid quietly ajar.
nodes.em5_s4_3_12: Dressed in crisp surgical scrubs with her long hair neatly tucked inside a cap and a mask over her face, Hospital Director Asuka Shiromiya stepped lightly inside, taking her place on the observation step well outside the yellow sterile boundary line.
nodes.em5_s4_3_13: (Catching sight of her out of the corner of her eye, blinking slightly) "...Director Asuka?"
nodes.em5_s4_3_14: (Eyes curving into a smile as she gave an easy wave) "Don't mind me—carry right on. I'm a surgeon too, after all; with two rooms running a synchronized adult living-donor liver transplant, there's no way I'd miss observing a case this compelling."
nodes.em5_s4_3_15: Carrying no evaluation clipboard and putting on zero administrative airs, she simply clasped her hands behind her back, watching with keen surgical interest as Ryuji securely ligated each variceal vessel along the edematous cirrhotic margin.
nodes.em5_s4_3_16: Only during a brief few-second lull while Hiroko swapped in fresh warm-saline laparotomy pads did Asuka speak up gently:
nodes.em5_s4_3_17: "Dr. Sakaguchi, the recipient's portal pressure looks even higher than preoperative imaging suggested. Rather than rushing to loop a Pringle tape around the hepatoduodenal ligament, are you planning to mobilize the bare area first?"
nodes.em5_s4_3_18: (Answering steadily without a tremor in his hands) "Yes. Chronic inflammatory edema around Naomi's hilum is severe—manipulating the pedicle too early would only stir up avoidable venous oozing and prolong subsequent clamping time. Better to clear the suprahepatic caval plane and right adrenal vein cleanly first, then dissect the first porta in one decisive pass right as the graft next door nears completion."
nodes.em5_s4_3_19: (Genuine admiration glinting in her eyes as she gave a light nod) "Pacing every step to the donor transection next door—protecting the recipient's coagulation reserve without chasing reckless speed... Beautifully orchestrated."
nodes.em5_s4_3_20: Right on cue, the green indicator on the wall-mounted inter-room intercom lit up with the crisp report of Room 1's circulating nurse—
nodes.em5_s4_3_21: "Room 1 reporting to Room 2! Chief Mido has completed intraoperative ultrasound mapping—the middle hepatic vein trunk remains preserved in full within the donor's left remnant liver, CUSA parenchymal transection has reached eighty percent, donor vitals are rock-stable, and right-lobe vascular pedicle division is projected in twenty minutes!"
nodes.em5_s4_3_22: (Gaze sharpening) "Right on the mark. Miyama, Hiroko—moving into fine dissection of the recipient first porta now. Prepare to receive the graft!"
nodes.em5_s4_3_23: As the operation entered its decisive window, Asuka fell tactfully silent in the observation zone, eyes fixed intently on the surgical field.
nodes.em5_s5_1_01: Inside Operating Room 1's back-table ice basin, the supple, healthy right-lobe graft was completing clear portal-vein flushing in 4-degree preservation solution.
nodes.em5_s5_1_02: At the donor table, Emiko Mido did not rush next door behind the flushed graft. Wielding bipolar forceps and fine atraumatic suture herself, she verified every microscopic bile radicle and venous tributary across Haruko Takase's left remnant cut surface until not a single drop oozed, confirmed vigorous middle hepatic vein and left hepatic artery waveforms on intraoperative Doppler ultrasound, and only then turned to her senior donor first assistant:
nodes.em5_s5_1_03: "Donor remnant cut surface shows zero oozing and zero bile leak; middle hepatic vein outflow is wide open, and cholangiography shows no stricture. I've set the drain position—layered closure and emergence handoff are under your primary charge. Call me instantly at the slightest change."
nodes.em5_s5_1_04: "Understood! Leave donor Haruko Takase to us for a smooth finish—go ahead to Room 2 with peace of mind, Chief!"
nodes.em5_s5_1_05: Having verified beyond doubt that the healthy donor was safely across every hazard line, Emiko stripped off her first sterile gown and gloves and strode briskly into the scrub corridor linking Operating Room 2.
nodes.em5_s5_2_01: Inside Operating Room 2, Naomi's nodular cirrhotic native liver had been cleanly explanted in full, the anhepatic timer ticking quietly on the wall as the sterile ice basin carrying the right-lobe graft arrived beside the Mayo stand.
nodes.em5_s5_2_02: Through the viewing pane between the scrub bay and Operating Room 2, Emiko—midway through a thorough surgical re-scrub—caught sight of Asuka Shiromiya standing outside the yellow line.
nodes.em5_s5_2_03: Lathering antiseptic soap across her forearms, Emiko's fingertips paused imperceptibly for half a second.
nodes.em5_s5_2_04: (Why is Director Asuka standing in Room 2 in person...? Could she be using the hospital's centerpiece transplant of the year to evaluate candidates for the next Chief of Surgery?)
nodes.em5_s5_2_05: The thought lingered for barely an instant before she dismissed it cleanly. Rinsing away the foam, she stepped into Room 2, let Itsumi Sonoda gown and glove her in fresh sterile gear, and took a quiet observation spot beside Kaori Miyama—reaching for not a single instrument in Ryuji's hands.
nodes.em5_s5_2_06: "Donor Haruko's remnant perfusion is intact, and Room 1 is safely closing. Sakaguchi—how is your outflow tract looking?"
nodes.em5_s5_2_07: "Right hepatic vein caval orifice venoplasty is widened and ready, and anhepatic hemodynamics are stable. Implanting the graft now—Hiroko, 5-0 Prolene vascular suture!"
nodes.em5_s5_2_09: Beneath the shadowless lamps, Ryuji cradled the prepared right-lobe graft in both hands and seated it smoothly into Naomi's right subphrenic fossa.
nodes.em5_s5_2_10: With Miyama maintaining chilled-pad cooling and crisp suction, Ryuji's wrists moved steady as clockwork—completing a wide, watertight continuous everting anastomosis between the right hepatic vein and inferior vena cava before aligning the donor and recipient main portal veins.
nodes.em5_s5_2_11: "Hepatic venous outflow and portal vein anastomoses complete, flushing and de-airing finished—Anesthesia, watch blood pressure and serum potassium closely. Releasing the portal clamp now—graft reperfusion!"
nodes.em5_s5_2_12: As the atraumatic vascular clamp eased open, dark crimson portal blood surged into the pale, chilled parenchyma. Within scarcely a dozen seconds, the entire transplanted lobe blushed evenly into vibrant, warm dusky rose, rising and falling gently with each breath!
nodes.em5_s5_2_13: "Minimal reperfusion syndrome! Invasive arterial pressure 106 over 64, heart rate 78, central venous pressure steady!"
nodes.em5_s5_2_14: "Thank goodness... The graft pinked right up in an instant!"
nodes.em5_s5_2_15: Yet the sharpest test of the blade had only just arrived.
nodes.em5_s5_2_16: As Ryuji flipped down his high-power microsurgical loupes to begin the delicate hepatic artery anastomosis, Kaori Miyama gently suctioned trace fluid deep in the hilum, her expression tightening beneath her mask:
nodes.em5_s5_2_17: "Dr. Sakaguchi... Years of autoimmune inflammation and portal-hypertensive edema have left the recipient's proper hepatic artery intima far more friable than expected—and the graft's right hepatic arterial stump is relatively short. Forcing a direct end-to-end pull to the native right hepatic stump will create excessive tension and risk postoperative hepatic artery thrombosis!"
nodes.em5_s5_2_18: Should the hepatic artery thrombose, the newly reperfused graft would suffer catastrophic biliary necrosis.
nodes.em5_s5_2_19: Standing at the side, Emiko's gaze sharpened and she started to speak—only to see Ryuji already pause his microneedle holder on his own, slipping a moist sterile fingertip with feather-light precision behind the recipient common hepatic duct toward the deep gastroduodenal bifurcation—
nodes.em5_s5_2_20: Every nuance of how he palpated the pulse and separated the deep periadventitial planes mirrored, down to the millimeter, the tactile feel he had honed on Emiko herself in Operating Room 1 six nights earlier.
nodes.em5_c3a_01: "We don't force an edematous distal stump to meet the graft. Miyama, retract the bile duct medially with feather-light tension—I'm carrying a bloodless periadventitial dissection 1.5 centimeters farther down along the lateral aspect and fashioning a wide branch-patch cuff at the gastroduodenal bifurcation so the anastomosis sits at zero tension."
nodes.em5_c3b_01: "Those friable, edematous distal millimeters can't stay. Miyama, guard the anterior wall of the portal vein posteriorly—I'll release the dense fibrous collar tethering the artery behind the bile duct first to free extra length, then step back to healthy intima at the bifurcation plane for a beveled anastomosis."
nodes.em5_s5m_01: Every person in the theater held their breath.
nodes.em5_s5m_02: Barely two millimeters across, the slender artery pulsed beneath the microsurgical loupes. Guiding microneedle holders and hair-fine 8-0 non-absorbable monofilament clear of the fragile edematous intima, Ryuji placed one stitch, two, three... eight interrupted full-thickness everting sutures, every bite and knot tensioned with instrument-grade uniformity.
nodes.em5_s5m_03: The instant the microvascular clamps clicked open—
nodes.em5_s5m_04: Bright arterial blood leaped across the anastomosis, setting the graft's right hepatic artery pulsing with vigorous elasticity! Seconds later, even before the duct-to-duct biliary anastomosis was begun, clear golden droplets of bile began welling naturally from the open orifice of the donor bile duct!
nodes.em5_s5m_05: Beyond the yellow line, Asuka Shiromiya—who had watched in quiet absorption until now—broke into a radiant smile and asked:
nodes.em5_s5m_06: "The second you spotted excessive tension at the native stump, Dr. Sakaguchi, you didn't hesitate for a beat before freeing deep length along the outer adventitial plane. In tissue that edematous, how did you judge the exact sheath depth without nicking a single intimal microvessel?"
nodes.em5_s5m_07: Above their masks, Ryuji's eyes met Emiko Mido's across the table for a fleeting instant:
nodes.em5_s5m_08: "Because not long ago, a singularly exacting colleague made sure my hands reviewed every layer of the hilar arterial sheath in person."
nodes.em5_s5m_09: At the side of the table, Emiko didn't smile, keeping her characteristically exacting gaze trained on the intraoperative Doppler spectrum as she deliberately posed the sharpest technical question in the room:
nodes.em5_s5m_10: "Anastomotic resistive index 0.62—nothing to fault on the waveform. Tell me, though: when you mobilized the bifurcation just now, how much margin did you preserve on the 9-o'clock peribiliary microvascular plexus along the common hepatic duct? If she develops ischemic biliary stricture postop, don't expect me to co-sign a passing grade."
nodes.em5_s5m_11: "Every millimeter of arterial mobilization hugged the left adventitial plane; electrocautery never once touched the fibrofatty vascular mesentery along the right bile duct margin, the arterial anastomosis sits tension-free, both donor and recipient duct ends are bleeding bright red, and golden bile is flowing steadily. Chief Mido is welcome to inspect it herself."
nodes.em5_s5m_12: Leaning in, Emiko examined the dry, vigorously pulsing hepatic artery anastomosis alongside the well-perfused donor bile duct steadily secreting clear golden bile, falling silent for two full seconds.
nodes.em5_s5m_13: Then she straightened slowly, the frost across her brow smoothing away completely:
nodes.em5_s5m_14: "...Hmph. Consider that a pass. On today's table, there really isn't a single thing left to nitpick."
nodes.em5_s5m_15: Watching the seamless give-and-take between the two leads—and the clockwork coordination of Miyama, Hiroko, and Sonoda—Asuka clapped her palms together softly in the observation area:
nodes.em5_s5m_16: "Crisp, spotless donor harvesting, rock-solid recipient vascular reconstruction, and two operating rooms meshing as though guided by a single pair of hands. Coming up here today was well worth it—I won't intrude on your final biliary anastomosis, closure, and ICU handoff. Magnificent work, both primary surgeons!"
nodes.em5_s5m_17: Giving the room a breezy wave, Asuka pushed open the side door and took her leave.
nodes.em5_s5m_18: Beneath the lamps, the Room 2 team carried that momentum straight through the final reconstructive step. Switching to 6-0 absorbable monofilament, Ryuji fashioned a tension-free end-to-end anastomosis between the graft right hepatic duct and the recipient common hepatic duct, verifying rich anastomotic perfusion, wide luminal patency, and zero bile staining on white-gauze inspection; only after seating subphrenic and Winslow drains and hearing Hiroko and Sonoda confirm three complete surgical counts did he begin layered closure of the abdominal wall.
nodes.em5_s5m_19: Forty minutes later, Operating Room 1 sent word first that Haruko Takase had been smoothly extubated awake and transferred safely to postoperative intensive care; and in Operating Room 2, as Ryuji tied off the final stitch on Naomi's abdominal incision, the dual-room living-donor liver transplant half a year in the making was officially crowned a complete bilateral success.
nodes.em5_s6_1_01: Several evenings later, quiet warmth filled the transplant recovery ward.
nodes.em5_s6_1_02: Both young women in the adjacent beds had already been stepped down from ICU lines and rested propped against raised headboards. Most of the preoperative sallow duskiness had faded from Naomi Miyahara's cheeks; turning her head toward the neighboring bed where Haruko Takase was idly counting IV drips, she spoke softly:
nodes.em5_s6_1_03: "Haruko. Ever since we stepped out of intensive care, I've wanted to say this to you properly—this truly isn't an ordinary favor. You saved my life. That is an immense grace."
nodes.em5_s6_1_04: (Ears turning bright red in an instant like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, waving both hands in a fluster) "W-wait a second, Naomi, don't hit me with such solemn lines out of nowhere—sshh, ow-ow-ow!!"
nodes.em5_s6_1_05: Waving too abruptly tugged straight across her right upper-abdominal incision; clutching the sterile dressing beneath her hospital gown with a sharp hiss, she took two seconds to catch her breath before muttering shyly with flushed cheeks:
nodes.em5_s6_1_06: "I don't want to be put on some pedestal as your life-saving benefactor! I just happened to be right beside you when you got sick, and later the tests proved my blood type and liver happened to suit you... What matters most to me is that we go right on being best friends like always—don't you dare think about owing me something every time you look at me!"
nodes.em5_s6_1_07: Naomi blinked, a gentle, relieved smile warming her eyes as she slipped effortlessly back into her familiar tone of keeping her scatterbrained roommate in check:
nodes.em5_s6_1_08: "All right—just like always. Then Miss Takase can start by setting that flailing hand neatly back on her blanket before she loosens her dressing. As for the ten years of late-night snacks we agreed on outside the OR, plus twenty years of homemade bentos on top, I won't shortchange you a single meal."
nodes.em5_s6_1_09: (Beaming at once, though daring only a tiny nod so as not to pull her stitches) "Now we're talking!"
nodes.em5_s6_1_10: Right then, two light knocks sounded at the ward door.
nodes.em5_s6_1_11: Emiko Mido stepped in first with ward charts tucked under her arm, Ryuji Sakaguchi right beside her as the pair entered for evening joint rounds.
nodes.em5_s6_1_12: "Sounds like spirits are high in here—we could hear you two chatting from the hall."
nodes.em5_s6_1_13: Stepping to Naomi's bedside first, Emiko scanned the bedside vitals flowsheet and drain graduations with practiced precision, her tone crisp and clinical without feeling cold:
nodes.em5_s6_1_14: "Miss Miyahara, since transitioning to clear liquids this afternoon, have you noticed any nausea, bloating, or unusual right-upper-quadrant distension?"
nodes.em5_s6_1_15: "None at all, Dr. Mido, Dr. Sakaguchi. Breathing feels much easier today than two days ago, and my stomach felt comfortable after the rice broth."
nodes.em5_s6_1_16: "Bedside Doppler looked great as well—both portal and arterial flows in the graft are crisp. Just ease into bedside mobilization step by step with your rehab plan."
nodes.em5_s6_1_17: Having cleared the recipient, Emiko turned to Haruko Takase's bed, lowering her gaze to inspect the clean, dry border of her right subcostal dressing:
nodes.em5_s6_1_18: "And you, Miss Takase? How bad is the incisional pain today when turning over or doing deep-breathing exercises?"
nodes.em5_s6_1_19: Facing the commanding Surgical Chief, Haruko reflexively sat a fraction straighter. Before she could laugh it off, Emiko closed her chart binder and looked straight into her eyes with unmistakable gravity:
nodes.em5_s6_1_20: "There is one more thing I need to tell you in person on rounds. Six months ago in clinic, you were frightened enough that your legs barely carried you out the door—yet after researching every surgical risk for yourself, you walked back in alone and saw six months of screening through without blinking. That clear-eyed courage deserves my earnest praise."
nodes.em5_s6_1_21: (Blushing bright crimson from the tip of her nose down to her collarbone, shrinking her shoulders in flustered embarrassment) "E-ehhh?! Dr. Mido, please don't praise me with such a straight face out of nowhere... That's even more embarrassing than Naomi thanking me a minute ago!"
nodes.em5_s6_1_22: (The corner of her lips curving by a whisper) "Merely stating a fact. In my department, I don't spare anyone when points come off—and I don't hold back when praise is earned."
nodes.em5_s6_1_23: Scratching her warm cheek, Haruko let her tense shoulders drop and finally murmured an honest admission:
nodes.em5_s6_1_24: "Though to tell the truth, Dr. Mido... once the anesthesia wore off, surgery really does hurt pretty badly..."
nodes.em5_s6_1_25: "With an open right subcostal incision that long, early postoperative pain couldn't be more normal—there is zero need to play tough and grit your teeth through it. I'll have the ward nurses step your multimodal analgesia up a notch tonight; getting solid sleep comes first if you want your remnant liver regenerating briskly."
nodes.em5_s6_1_26: At the mention of the incision, Haruko glanced down at the long dressing across her abdomen, hesitated for two beats, and couldn't resist asking in a small voice:
nodes.em5_s6_1_27: "Um... Dr. Mido, may I ask one more thing... With a cut this long across my stomach, is it going to leave a really obvious scar afterward? Once Naomi is all better, I still want to go back to the beach with her..."
nodes.em5_s6_1_28: Without brushing the worry aside for a second, Emiko answered with complete professionalism:
nodes.em5_s6_1_29: "Your abdominal wall was closed to our hospital's highest precision layered-suture standard, with subcutaneous tension thoroughly offloaded and clean epidermal apposition. You are still in early postoperative healing right now, so don't judge by how it looks today—once the scar matures over the coming months, the line will fade substantially on its own. And if a noticeable mark still bothers you later on, our hospital can arrange dedicated late-stage scar revision—when recovery goes ideally, it becomes barely noticeable in everyday life."
nodes.em5_s6_1_32: From the neighboring bed, Naomi watched her best friend's lively profile and smiled:
nodes.em5_s6_1_33: "Once both of us have fully recovered, let's head back to the beach—and properly finish the trip that got cut short six months ago."
nodes.em5_s6_1_34: "Deal! Hold me to it—train tickets and seaside shaved ice are both on you this time!"
nodes.em5_s6_1_35: "Fine, fine, my treat. Just stop bouncing around right now before Dr. Mido docks your recovery score."
nodes.em5_s6_1_36: Listening to the familiar lively bickering resume behind her, Emiko signed her name briskly across both progress charts, a whisper-faint yet unmistakable warmth crossing her cool eyes.
nodes.em5_s6_2_01: Stepping quietly out of the ward and easing the door shut, the two surgeons walked side by side past the hushed corner of the floor and paused before the floor-to-ceiling window at the end of the surgical corridor. Dusk was gathering outside as city lights blinked on one after another in the distance.
nodes.em5_s6_2_02: "Naomi's transaminases and bilirubin came down nearly into the normal range this afternoon, and Haruko's remnant regeneration markers look textbook. Back in Operating Room 2, both your arterial bifurcation patchplasty and your hemostasis calls after reperfusion were clean."
nodes.em5_s6_2_03: "If Room 1 hadn't preserved the graft's right hepatic artery and biliary hilar plate intact up front while keeping cold ischemia under forty minutes, steady hands alone wouldn't have made my side nearly that smooth. We won that case across two rooms together."
nodes.em5_s6_2_04: Emiko turned her head to look at him—and unlike their earlier days, she didn't assign an "85" or "88" to the operation.
nodes.em5_s6_2_05: Leaning lightly against the sill with her arms folded, she let a quiet moment pass before speaking in the same clear, composed cadence she used when assigning cases in the department:
nodes.em5_s6_2_06: "Sakaguchi. Regarding the hospital's next Chief of Surgery—I don't intend to compete with you for that post anymore."
nodes.em5_s6_2_07: Blinking in surprise, Ryuji turned to face her squarely:
nodes.em5_s6_2_09: "Don't misunderstand me. I am certainly not conceding that my blade is inferior to yours—and I haven't lost my head over the two of us being lovers in private and decided to hand you a title. On the donor hepatectomy in Room 1, my work wasn't half a step behind yours."
nodes.em5_s6_2_10: "Nobody knows that better than I do. Then why say this all of a sudden?"
nodes.em5_s6_2_11: Emiko looked down the far end of the corridor toward the twin lit doors of the surgical suite, her gaze candid and sharp:
nodes.em5_s6_2_12: "I used to believe the only way to uphold this department's highest standard was to sit in the Chief's chair myself and hold final sign-off over every high-risk operation in my own hands."
nodes.em5_s6_2_13: "Yet from lying beneath your scalpel last week listening to you call variant vessels, to standing guard over two separate operating rooms to bring those two young women back... for the first time, it struck me that two tables were meant to have someone answering for each of them all along."
nodes.em5_s6_2_14: Drawing her gaze back, she met Ryuji's eyes straight on—every ounce of her pride intact, now paired with an unhurried poise she had never shown before:
nodes.em5_s6_2_15: "What a Chief of Surgery shoulders is the talent pipeline, resource allocation, and the long-range direction of the entire department over years to come; and nobody knows me better than I know myself—where I truly want to pour every drop of my focus is standing squarely beneath the shadowless lamp with a scalpel in hand, holding the front-line standard of every operating room in this department without compromise. Staying on as Surgical Chief to guard the tables while you, if it comes to pass, stand in the Chief of Surgery's spot coordinating the whole picture... that division of labor strikes me as far more worthwhile—for Hoshimi's Department of Surgery and for the two of us—than fighting to claim the title alone."
nodes.em5_c4a_01: "'If'? Here I thought with Chief Mido actually giving me her backing, the Chief of Surgery post was practically locked up."
nodes.em5_c4a_02: (Giving a cool scoff and shooting him an unsparing look) "Of course 'if.' Did you think naming Hoshimi Hospital's Chief of Surgery is something my word alone decides? Plenty of sharp eyes in this hospital are still watching you, and tougher cases than this are waiting ahead—don't celebrate prematurely."
nodes.em5_c4b_01: "If that day really comes, having a Surgical Chief stricter than the department head policing operative quality beside me means I won't dare slack off for a single morning."
nodes.em5_c4b_02: (Lips curving slightly) "Naturally. And let's be clear up front: all I'm doing is stepping out of a head-to-head race against you—whether you clear the hospital's remaining hurdles and actually earn the chair is entirely up to your own ability. Don't expect any backdoor favors from me."
nodes.em5_s6m_01: Straightening from the windowsill, Emiko reached out and smoothed a barely perceptible crease from the lapel of Ryuji's white coat. Her fingertips lingered at his collar for one brief second before she resumed her crisp, no-nonsense Chief's demeanor:
nodes.em5_s6m_02: "And don't let two words of praise today go to your head. On tomorrow morning's routine list, if I catch your suture margin off by even a single millimeter, I will call your name out in front of the entire morning conference just the same."
nodes.em5_s6m_03: (Smiling) "Wouldn't have it any other way, Chief Mido."
nodes.em5_s6m_04: Golden evening light stretched across their backs as they walked down the corridor side by side—with no need left to rank one above the other, two pairs of hands kept hold of their own edge, striding toward the next operation they would stand through together.
